    "chain": "route (Old French rute, from Latin rupta via) = broken way; harvest (Old English hærfest) = autumn, season of reaping",
    "reading": "A broken path through the season of reaping; the way is cut, the yield is gathered.",

    "languages": ["en", "de"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Route (fr. route = road) + 91 (fr. quatre-vingt-onze = four-twenty-eleven) + Harvest (fr. récolte, but 'harvest' sounds like 'her vest' in en)",
    "reading": "Road of four-twenty-eleven; her vest is the gathered cloth of the field.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",

    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "R = regina (queen), 91 = 9+1 = 10 = J (Yod), H = hortus (garden) — R91H",
    "reading": "Queen of the garden of the ten; the tenth letter is the hand of God.",
    "languages": ["la", "he"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "R = road, 9 = nine (nun, fish in Aramaic), 1 = one (aleph, ox), H = hedge, harvest = sickle",
    "reading": "Road of the fish and the ox, hedged by the sickle's cut.",
    "languages": ["en", "he", "arc"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "Route = 9 (R) + 1 (oute? no, but 91 = 9+1=10, 10 = perfection; Harvest = H=8, A=1, R=18, V=22, E=5, S=19, T=20 = 93, 9+3=12, 1+2=3",
    "reading": "The perfect ten leads to the three; the harvest's sum is the trinity.",
    "languages": ["en", "he"],
    "source": "generative",

  },
  {

    "chain": "harvest (Old English hærfest) cognate with Latin carpere (to pluck), Greek karpos (fruit); route from rupta (broken)",
    "reading": "The broken way of plucking; the fruit is taken from the ruptured path.",
    "languages": ["en", "la", "grc"],
    "source": "OED; Pokorny's Indogermanisches Etymologisches Wörterbuch",
    "confidence": 0.7
  }
